failure_summary.description: Agents missed new constraints, skipped a pending domain, or treated an unmet follow-up as already complete.
Agents omitted required result saves or cache retrievals, nested a cache call, reused unavailable variables, or imported and redefined runtime models.
A non-proximity area question triggered an invalid search_nearest call with only one result domain.
The return date was incorrectly added as an outbound arrival-date constraint, and user-provided dates were unnecessarily converted.

patch.reasoning: Most observed errors already violate explicit skill rules, so repeating those rules would not fill a gap. Add guidance for the uncovered case where a user replaces an earlier same-domain preference, and specify search_nearest's required result-domain count to prevent the observed validation error.

edits.target: Return no-planning only when every requested or pending deliverable reflects all current constraints and the latest turn adds no request, accepted offer, or new constraint.
edits.content: When the user explicitly corrects or replaces a prior same-domain criterion (for example, “actually,” “instead,” or “only”), treat the conflicting earlier criterion as superseded. Do not filter a result narrowed by that superseded criterion; search afresh using the replacement and other currently active explicit criteria, and save the result.

edits.target: Use `search_nearest` only when the user asks about proximity, with relevant domain results and `groupBy` set to the requested anchor domain.
edits.content: `search_nearest` requires exactly two result-domain arguments among `hotels`, `attractions`, and `restaurants`; do not call it with only one result or more than two.
